lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Consider leading with experience rather than education if applying after gaining more post-MBA experience.
items.because: Education near the top makes more sense for a current MBA student or recent graduate.

items.says: Move Harbor Payments above Crestline Logistics.
items.because: Experience is generally listed in reverse chronological order, and Harbor is more recent.

items.says: Make sure the profile link is clickable in the submitted file.
Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They aren’t needed for most applications and can invite irrelevant bias.

items.says: Make the MBA degree status clear for the version submitted.
items.because: The degree may still be in progress, or its listed completion date may have passed.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the rate calculation rather than showing that late deliveries fell.
items.because: The bullet may look like it improved the metric by changing its definition, not by improving service.

items.says: Add the measurement period for the 30% reduction.
Add the baseline or absolute pick-error rate if available.
Clarify how the redesign, rollout and retraining contributed to the result.
items.because: The relationship among those actions is hard to follow.

items.says: Explain or spell out “S&OP.”
items.because: Some readers may not know the abbreviation.

items.says: Clarify how forecast error was measured if the figure needs context.
Say whether the 1,800 hours are measured savings or an annualized estimate.
Add evidence of adoption or operational effect beyond training if available.
items.because: It would make the impact easier to assess.

items.says: Specify whether the 35% improvement is relative or a percentage-point increase.
Give the measurement period or comparison basis for checkout conversion.
Verify or clarify the “all merchants” scope.
items.because: It may appear inconsistent with the later 2,300-merchant pilot unless these were separate initiatives.

items.says: Clarify the plan or milestone behind “two weeks ahead of plan.”
items.because: It may not be obvious to an outside reader.

items.says: State the currency of the 1.1 million figure.
Make clear what period the 1.1 million figure covers.
Clarify what the 1.1 million figure represents.
items.because: It is difficult to tell whether it is the estimated annual loss, the value of the opportunity, or something else.

items.says: Standardize “analysed” for the target market.
items.because: The résumé uses U.S. locations but mixes spelling conventions.

items.says: Add a timeframe or baseline for the queue reduction if available.
Show the effect on merchant onboarding or support, not just ticket volume.
items.because: Ticket volume alone is less persuasive than that effect.

items.says: Do not treat the opt-in comparison as evidence that the redesign caused a difference without accounting for selection bias.
items.because: Merchants chose whether to use the new flow, so the comparison is not a controlled test.

items.says: Report a finding or avoid keeping this as a standalone achievement.
items.because: The bullet gives no result.

items.says: Clarify whether the pilot result was measured against a comparable baseline.
Clarify whether “median time to first payment” has the same definition across the groups or periods compared.
Clarify what “launched to 3,100 students” measures.
items.because: It could mean availability, registrations, or active use.

items.says: Explain how the 9 tonnes of food were measured.
Make sure “in its first year” matches the project dates.
Standardize “tonnes” for the target market.
items.because: The résumé uses U.S. locations but mixes units.

items.says: Add the measurement period for weekly active user growth.
Clarify whether user growth was linked to reminders or merely followed them.
items.because: The bullet should not imply causation without evidence.

items.says: Add the timeframe for the 95% pickup-slot fill rate.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it held consistently or reflects a short snapshot.

items.says: Give the comparison period for the reduction in staff cover shifts.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it held consistently or reflects a short snapshot.

items.says: Add a deliverable, decision or operational change from the working sessions if supportable.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity but not a result.

items.says: Replace the passive phrasing with a clear account of what you personally did.
items.because: The current wording obscures your role.

items.says: Clarify how much the intake form changed.
Explain what adoption by front-desk staff meant in practice.
Include an outcome if one was measured.
The merchant-onboarding bullet duplicates a Harbor Payments achievement.
items.because: It looks like a copy-and-paste error and could undermine confidence in the résumé.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding bullet conflicts with the hospital-practicum context.
items.because: It refers to merchants, not a hospital network.

items.says: Keep A/B testing only if you have genuine controlled-experiment experience.
items.because: The Harbor opt-in comparison is not necessarily an A/B test.

items.says: Prioritize skills most relevant to the target roles.
items.because: The skills list is fairly generic.

items.says: List only tools you can use confidently and that matter for the target roles.
